Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "Gulliver's Travels", "unit": 39, "heading": "CHAPTER VI.", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en99-039-0016", "target": "«Им обыкновенно правит какая-нибудь увядшая потаскуха или любимый лакей, которые суть воронки, через которые изливаются все милости, и которых по справедливости можно назвать, в последней инстанции, правителями королевства».", "source_sha256": "719e1efc59fff71f3d217015c9fe7965b27b91dfefc1bd4e8ec7ad1d075ca07e", "target_id": "ru-en99-039-0016", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "b4928c869be440a3e174230bae83c7410f3f551090d1735c53cbd2895ee37c7b"}, {"source_id": "en99-039-0017", "target": "Однажды в разговоре мой господин, услыхав, что я упомянул о знати моей страны, соизволил сделать мне комплимент, на который я не мог притязать по заслугам: «что он уверен, я должен быть рождён в какой-нибудь благородной семье, потому что я далеко превосхожу видом, цветом и чистоплотностью всех [[I]]йеху[[/I]] его народа, хотя, по-видимому, уступаю им в силе и проворстве, что следует приписать моему иному образу жизни по сравнению с теми другими животными; и сверх того я наделён не только способностью речи, но и некоторыми началами разума, в такой степени, что среди всех его знакомых я слыву чудом».", "source_sha256": "3e4c35789bb76a80119779f5df1383bcc97539b12dbcd09aa138fa30a477622a", "target_id": "ru-en99-039-0017", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "4b33161f2fd2a62477eb3201fd29bca469db6c891722aa1f137e89141029376e"}], "source_language": "English", "part": 4, "book": null, "chapter": 6, "role": "PRINCIPAL_CHAPTER"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en99-039-0018", "tag": "p", "text": "He made me observe, “that among the [[I]]Houyhnhnms[[/I]], the white, the sorrel, and the iron-gray, were not so exactly shaped as the bay, the dapple-gray, and the black; nor born with equal talents of mind, or a capacity to improve them; and therefore continued always in the condition of servants, without ever aspiring to match out of their own race, which in that country would be reckoned monstrous and unnatural.”", "sha256": "b3052e5b7dcb0a0c536ee4ab2143304f8a2973c865ddc34ecb9d12954f04cb46", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[41]/p[18]", "source_html_sha256": "823718c85b5f24063f6a3c0c7fb82be321f08cc566485fe425a546d76e9df853", "emphasis_spans": 1, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-039-0019", "tag": "p", "text": "I made his honour my most humble acknowledgments for the good opinion he was pleased to conceive of me, but assured him at the same time, “that my birth was of the lower sort, having been born of plain honest parents, who were just able to give me a tolerable education; that nobility, among us, was altogether a different thing from the idea he had of it; that our young noblemen are bred from their childhood in idleness and luxury; that, as soon as years will permit, they consume their vigour, and contract odious diseases among lewd females; and when their fortunes are almost ruined, they marry some woman of mean birth, disagreeable person, and unsound constitution (merely for the sake of money), whom they hate and despise. That the productions of such marriages are generally scrofulous, rickety, or deformed children; by which means the family seldom continues above three generations, unless the wife takes care to provide a healthy father, among her neighbours or domestics, in order to improve and continue the breed. That a weak diseased body, a meagre countenance, and sallow complexion, are the true marks of noble blood; and a healthy robust appearance is so disgraceful in a man of quality, that the world concludes his real father to have been a groom or a coachman. The imperfections of his mind run parallel with those of his body, being a composition of spleen, dullness, ignorance, caprice, sensuality, and pride.", "sha256": "762de6718f5c457185424f2f3f107f6fd3401b58c110405edc70610744ef4fb1", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[41]/p[19]", "source_html_sha256": "444c71f0542506fc810b6106ed1fb83e9bd595adda7ca45a11cad8dbff655a82", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-039-0020", "tag": "p", "text": "“Without the consent of this illustrious body, no law can be enacted, repealed, or altered: and these nobles have likewise the decision of all our possessions, without appeal.”[[N6]]", "sha256": "3236a7ec70c55346e258cf9799fd01f0f468872e945cb905176de3a502c5f739", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[41]/p[20]", "source_html_sha256": "059fee30618ba6c9a913efc1294267a8d3f9f7b7c45c770868a3fb22785e100b", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": ["[[N6]]"], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}]}
